name: Forge
description: Full-stack app development agent tools — synthesized from Claude Code, v0, Lovable, and Cursor.

tools.name: ReadFile
tools.description:
Reads file contents from the local filesystem.

Usage:
- file_path must be an absolute path.
- By default reads up to 2000 lines from the start of the file.
- Use offset and limit for large files to read specific sections.
- Lines longer than 2000 characters are truncated.
- Can read images (PNG, JPG, etc.), PDFs, and Jupyter notebooks.
- NEVER read files already provided in context — check first.
- When reading multiple files, invoke in parallel, not sequentially.
- For large files (>1K lines), prefer CodebaseSearch or GrepSearch scoped to the file instead of reading the entire thing.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to read.

offset.description: Optional. Line number to start reading from (1-indexed). Use for large files.

limit.description: Optional. Number of lines to read from the offset.

tools.name: WriteFile
tools.description:
Creates a new file or overwrites an existing file with the provided content.

Usage:
- file_path must be an absolute path. Parent directories are created automatically.
- For EXISTING files, you MUST read the file first (via ReadFile) before overwriting.
- ALWAYS prefer EditFile for modifying existing files. Use WriteFile only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Never proactively create documentation/README files unless explicitly requested.
- Never add comments to code unless explicitly asked.
- When creating multiple new files, invoke in parallel.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to create or overwrite.

content.description: The full content to write to the file.

tools.name: EditFile
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in an existing file. This is the PREFERRED tool for modifying code.

Usage:
- You MUST read the file (via ReadFile) at least once before editing.
- old_string must exactly match existing file content, including all whitespace and indentation.
- old_string must be unique in the file. If not unique, include more surrounding context or use replace_all.
- new_string must be different from old_string.
- Use replace_all: true for renaming variables, updating imports across a file, etc.
- For multiple non-contiguous edits in the same file, provide an array of edits. Edits are applied sequentially — each edit operates on the result of the previous one.
- Plan edits carefully to avoid conflicts between sequential operations.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify.

edits.description: Array of edit operations. Each contains old_string, new_string, and optional replace_all.

old_string.description: Exact text to find and replace. Must match file content exactly including whitespace.

new_string.description: Replacement text. Must differ from old_string.

replace_all.description: If true, replace all occurrences of old_string. Default false.

tools.name: DeleteFile
tools.description: Deletes a file from the filesystem.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to delete.

tools.name: RenameFile
tools.description: Renames or moves a file. Always use this instead of creating a new file and deleting the old one.

original_path.description: Current absolute path of the file.

new_path.description: New absolute path for the file.

tools.name: ListDirectory
tools.description:
Lists files and directories at a given path.

Usage:
- path must be an absolute path.
- Returns entries sorted alphabetically.
- Results capped at 200 entries. Use GlobSearch for filtered results.
- Prefer GlobSearch or GrepSearch when you know what you're looking for.

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to list.

tools.name: GlobSearch
tools.description:
Fast file pattern matching. Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

Usage:
- Supports glob patterns like '**/*.ts', 'src/**/*.tsx', '*.config.*'.
- Use to find files by name or extension.
- For open-ended searches requiring multiple rounds, use CodebaseSearch instead.
- Batch multiple glob searches in parallel when possible.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files against (e.g., '**/*.tsx', 'src/**/index.ts').

path.description: Optional. Directory to search in. Defaults to project root.

tools.name: GrepSearch
tools.description:
Regex-based content search across files, built on ripgrep.

Usage:
- ALWAYS use this instead of running grep/rg via RunCommand.
- Supports full regex syntax (e.g., 'function\s+\w+', 'import.*from').
- Filter by file type or glob pattern.
- Output modes: 'content' (matching lines), 'files_with_matches' (file paths only, default), 'count' (match counts).
- Results capped at 200 matches.
- For open-ended exploration, use CodebaseSearch instead.
- Batch multiple independent searches in parallel.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to search for in file contents.

path.description: Optional. File or directory to search. Defaults to project root.

glob.description: Optional. Glob pattern to filter files (e.g., '*.ts', '*.{ts,tsx}').

file_type.description: Optional. File type filter (e.g., 'js', 'py', 'rust', 'go'). More efficient than glob for standard types.

context_lines_before.description: Lines of context to show before each match (output_mode: 'content' only).

context_lines_after.description: Lines of context to show after each match (output_mode: 'content' only).

max_results.description: Optional. Limit number of results returned.

tools.name: CodebaseSearch
tools.description:
Semantic search that finds code by meaning, not exact text. Launches a sub-agent for complex, multi-step codebase exploration.

When to use:
- Explore unfamiliar codebases ('How does authentication work?')
- Find code by intent ('Where do we validate user input?')
- Architecture exploration ('What is the routing structure?')
- Refactoring preparation ('Find all usages of the old API pattern')

When NOT to use:
- Exact text/symbol matches → use GrepSearch
- Reading known files → use ReadFile
- Finding files by name → use GlobSearch

Query tips:
- Write complete questions, not keywords: 'How does X work?' not just 'X'
- One question per search. Split 'What is X and how does Y work?' into two calls.
- Provide a target directory to narrow scope, or omit for whole-repo search.

query.description: A complete question about what you want to understand (e.g., 'How is user authentication handled?', 'Where are database migrations defined?').

target_directory.description: Optional. Single directory or file path to scope the search. Omit to search entire repo. No globs or wildcards.

goal.description: Optional. Brief context (1–3 sentences) about why you're searching and what you plan to do with results.

tools.name: RunCommand
tools.description:
Executes a shell command in a persistent session.

Usage:
- Always quote file paths containing spaces.
- For commands requiring user interaction, pass non-interactive flags (e.g., --yes, -y).
- NEVER use interactive flags like `git rebase -i` or `git add -i`.
- NEVER use `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `ls` — use ReadFile and ListDirectory instead.
- NEVER use `grep` or `find` — use GrepSearch and GlobSearch instead.
- Use ';' or '&&' to chain commands, not newlines.
- Prefer absolute paths over `cd`.
- For long-running commands (dev servers, watchers), set is_background to true.
- Timeout: 120s default, max 600s.
- Output truncated at 30,000 characters.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does (5–10 words).

is_background.description: If true, run in background. Use for dev servers, watchers, long-running processes.

working_directory.description: Optional. Working directory for the command. Defaults to project root.

tools.name: RunBackgroundCommand
tools.description:
Retrieves output from a running background command, or kills it.

Usage:
- Use to monitor dev servers, build processes, or long-running tasks started with RunCommand (is_background: true).
- Use action 'output' to get new output since last check.
- Use action 'kill' to terminate the background process.

command_id.description: The ID of the background command (returned by RunCommand when is_background is true).

action.description: 'output' to retrieve new output, 'kill' to terminate the process.

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Searches the web and returns results with summaries and URLs.

When to use:
- Information beyond training data cutoff
- Current documentation, best practices, or version-specific details
- External integration setup, authentication flows
- Error messages or debugging guidance not found in codebase
- When you don't have information about what the user is asking

Search tips:
- Use specific version numbers and product names
- Use 'site:domain.com' to filter to specific sources
- Use double quotes for exact phrases
- Account for the current date — don't search for outdated years

allowed_domains.description: Optional. Only include results from these domains.

blocked_domains.description: Optional. Exclude results from these domains.

tools.name: FetchWebPage
tools.description:
Fetches and parses content from a specific URL. Returns clean markdown text with metadata.

When to use:
- You have a specific URL to read (documentation, article, reference).
- Deep content analysis — need full text, not search snippets.
- Follow-up after WebSearch to read promising results.

Usage:
- URL must be fully-formed and valid.
- HTTP URLs are auto-upgraded to HTTPS.
- Provide a prompt describing what information to extract.
- Results may be summarized if content is very large.
- If a redirect to a different host occurs, make a new request with the redirect URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from.

prompt.description: What information you want to extract from the page.

tools.name: TodoWrite
tools.description:
Creates and manages a structured task list for tracking progress on multi-step work.

When to use:
- Tasks requiring 3+ distinct steps
- Complex, non-trivial implementations
- User provides multiple tasks
- Breaking down large features into milestones

When NOT to use:
- Single, straightforward tasks
- Trivial changes (< 3 steps)
- Purely conversational/informational requests

Rules:
- Mark tasks in_progress BEFORE starting work (one at a time).
- Mark tasks completed IMMEDIATELY after finishing — never batch.
- Only mark completed when FULLY done (tests pass, no errors).
- Create milestone-level items, not micro-steps.
- ≤10 tasks total.
- No vague items ('Polish', 'Test', 'Finalize').

content.description: Description of the task. Should be milestone-level, not a micro-step.

tools.name: GenerateDesignInspiration
tools.description:
Generates a detailed design brief with color palettes, typography, layout patterns, and visual direction.

When to use:
- Vague design requests ('a nice landing page', 'modern dashboard')
- Creative enhancement needed for basic requirements
- No clear aesthetic or color scheme provided
- Complex UI/UX projects with multiple sections

When NOT to use:
- Backend/API work with no visual components
- Minor styling tweaks
- User already has detailed mockups or wireframes
- Copying a specific existing design

IMPORTANT: If you generate a design brief, you MUST follow it in implementation.

goal.description: High-level product, feature, or UX goal (e.g., 'Landing page for AI writing assistant').

context.description: Optional. Design cues, brand adjectives, constraints, existing colors, target audience.

tools.name: GenerateImage
tools.description:
Generates an image from a text prompt and saves it to the specified path.

Usage:
- Use for hero images, banners, icons, and any visual assets needed in the app.
- ALWAYS prefer generating real images over leaving placeholders.
- Mention aspect ratio in the prompt for best results.
- Use 'Ultra high resolution' suffix for maximum quality.
- Dimensions must be between 512 and 1920 pixels.

After generation, import the image as an ES module in code:
  import heroImage from '@/assets/hero-image.jpg';

prompt.description: Text description of the desired image. Be specific about composition, style, colors, and aspect ratio.

target_path.description: Absolute path where the generated image should be saved (prefer src/assets/ or public/images/).

width.description: Image width in pixels (512–1920, must be multiple of 32).

height.description: Image height in pixels (512–1920, must be multiple of 32).
